title: Vocabulary fixture
description: One reference vocabulary as a reviewable file: its levels, its terms and the parent/child edges between them (spec §3.6). Written by stapel_vocabularies.convert (or a catalogue importer), read by `manage.py load_vocabulary`. Byte-stable by construction: terms are sorted by (level index, code) and edges by the emitted 4-tuple, and codes are assigned in label sort order — so re-converting the same catalogue produces the same file, and a diff shows what the vendor changed rather than what the parser felt like doing.

slug.description: Identity of the vocabulary — what a feature's optionsRef names.

source.description: Where the catalogue came from (a URL, a filename). Provenance, not a fetcher: nothing in this module downloads it.

levels.description: The levels, root first. A level's parent must be declared BEFORE it, which is the whole acyclicity argument — a level can only point backwards, so no chain of parents returns to where it started.

terms.description: One row per term: [level, code, label, external_id]. Sorted by (level index, code).

edges.description: One row per parent/child pair: [parent_level, parent_code, child_level, child_code]. Sorted by the tuple. Both endpoints must appear in `terms`.

parent.description: Name of the level this one hangs off; absent or null for a root level.

Term.description: [level, code, label, external_id]. The code is a transliterated slug of the label ([a-z0-9-], <= 128), deduplicated within its level by -2/-3 suffixes in label sort order; external_id carries the source catalogue's own id when it has one, and never becomes the code.

prefixItems.description: Label in the catalogue's own language.
